## 8. The sentences of the specification

Changed, each before and after:
1. `Specification/appendices/changes.tex:5245-5248`. Before: "coercions generic over the four numbers from \TYP{NaturalNumeral} at its five integer types and from \TYP{RadixPointNumeral} at \EXP{\mathbb{R}64} and \EXP{\mathbb{R}32}". After: "coercions generic over the four numbers from \TYP{NaturalNumeral} at its five integer types, \EXP{\mathbb{R}64} and \EXP{\mathbb{R}32}, and from \TYP{RadixPointNumeral} at \EXP{\mathbb{R}64} and \EXP{\mathbb{R}32}".
2. `changes.tex:5259-5263`, added after "so a coercion that throws an exception stops the program.": "The compiled program initializes the class of its component, and after it the class of each component that it imports, before the program runs, inside a task on a pool of one thread of its own, so that a coercion whose body spawns a task, as an operator applied to two calls may, fills its place; the tasks that a coercion spawns there run one after another."
3. `changes.tex:5270-5272`. Before: "only when the place is evaluated: one outside an integer type's range, one at a type that declares no coercion". After: "only when the place is evaluated: one outside an integer type's range, one that rounds to an infinity of \EXP{\mathbb{R}64} or \EXP{\mathbb{R}32}, one at a type that declares no coercion".
4. `changes.tex:5277-5280`. Before: "It converts a numeral that rounds to an infinity of \EXP{\mathbb{R}64} or \EXP{\mathbb{R}32} into that infinity with no error (row~967); it converts a numeral at a parameter". After: "It refuses when it loads a program a numeral type written as a type that an object or a trait extends, or as a static argument. It converts a numeral at a parameter".
5. `changes.tex:5299`. Before: "row of the revival's gap ledger: the interpreter runs the operator of \EXP{\mathbb{R}64} where a floating-point numeral stands to the left of an \EXP{\mathbb{R}32} (row~958); the interpreter loads and runs a program that writes a numeral type as a type that an object or a trait extends, or as a static argument (row~974); a numeral with a radix point keeps only one of". After: "row of the revival's gap ledger: a numeral with a radix point keeps only one of".
6. `changes.tex:5306`. Before: "the coercion at each evaluation of the place (row~957); a coercion from a numeral type whose body spawns a task, as an operator applied to two calls may, stops the load of the class that holds the place, which the compiled program loads before it starts its tasks (row~971); where a \KWD{nat} or \KWD{int}". After: "the coercion at each evaluation of the place (row~957); where a \KWD{nat} or \KWD{int}".
7. `changes.tex:2717-2719`. Before: "and the result is an \EXP{\mathbb{R}32}; the interpreter departs where a floating-point numeral stands to the left of the \EXP{\mathbb{R}32}, and runs the operator of \EXP{\mathbb{R}64} (row~958 of the revival's gap ledger); an \EXP{\mathbb{R}32} is converted". Before: "The compiled path's own library declares no coercion into \EXP{\mathbb{R}64} from an integer type or from \TYP{NaturalNumeral}; there \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}, \EXP{\mathbb{N}32} and integer numerals convert to \EXP{\mathbb{R}64} only explicitly, and the other integer types not at all." After: "The compiled path's own library declares the coercion into \EXP{\mathbb{R}64} from \TYP{NaturalNumeral} and none from an integer type; there \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} and \EXP{\mathbb{N}32} convert to \EXP{\mathbb{R}64} only explicitly, and the other integer types not at all."

### P (`rung-forked-arguments`)

**The change.**

- *A call's arguments on the compiled path.* The team's code generator evaluates a tuple argument's elements in order, under its comment "Why isn't this parallel???" (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java`, `evalArg`, at the team's last commit a874948ac), while the specification gives each argument an implicit thread of its own (`Specification/basic/evaluation/parallelism.tex:60-64`) and walk forks them (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/Evaluator.java:342`). The tree now forks the arguments of a function call and of a dotted method call where the parallelism analyzer marked the argument tuple: two or more arguments that are calls of the program's named functions. So such arguments may run at once, their side effects in any order, and a compiled program must not rely on left-to-right arguments. Test: `compiler_tests/CallArgumentsForkCompiled`. Evidence: 'a function's two arguments: 1,2, at most 1 at once' before, 'at most 2 at once' after. The calls written in the compiler's prelude do not fork, so its `SUM` still runs one body at a time.
- *A group that throws, on the compiled path.* The team's code generator joins the forked arms of a `do … also`, a tuple or an operator on the normal path only (`CodeGen.java`, `genParallelExprs`, at a874948ac), so an arm ran on after its group had thrown; the specification has a group complete only when each of its threads has (`parallelism.tex:82-100`), and walk joins every arm (`Evaluator.java:275`). The tree now waits for every arm that was forked and then throws the exception of the first arm, in the arms' order, that threw; an arm that was never forked is not run. Test: `compiler_tests/AlsoArmThrowsJoinsCompiled`. Evidence: 'after the catch: flag 0, later: flag 1' before, 'flag 1, later: flag 1' after.

The tree compiles them. Tests: `compiler_tests/TaskArmLocalSlot`, `TryInArmRungG`, `AtomicEndsArmCompiled`. An `atomic` block or a `try` as a call's later argument that does not fork still fails so (`compiler_tests/XXXAtomicBlockLaterArgument`): bind its value in a statement of its own.
- *The parallel range under walk.* The team's library splits a parallel `ZZ32` range down to single elements, each a task (`Library/RangeInternals.fss`, `CompactFullParScalarRange`, at a874948ac). The tree stops the split at 16 elements and runs each chunk by the sequential range's methods (`Library/RangeInternals.fss:20`, `:1320-1321`, `:1337-1338`). So under walk a `for`, a comprehension or a reduction over a `lo#n` or `lo:hi` range of sixteen elements or fewer runs its bodies one after another, in index order, and a longer one in chunks of at most 16; a test of parallelism needs a range longer than 16, and a floating-point sum can differ in its last bits from the team's, since the chunks are summed in order. A range with a stride still splits to single elements. Test: `tests/ParRangeGrainWalk`. Evidence: the bodies of `0#16` ran '0 4 8 6 1 5 9 7 10 12 3 2 11 13 14 15' before and in index order after; the specification lets an implementation serialize any part of a group (`parallelism.tex:88-90`).

(* An atomic block answers at its commit for what its nested block read, where the nested block wrote nothing and where an exception left it: no update of another block is lost. atomic.tex, section "Atomic Expressions". *)
component XXXAtomicNestedReadsKeptWalk
export Executable

object Carry(q: ZZ32) extends UncheckedException end

x: ZZ32 := 0
u: ZZ32 := 0

readX(): ZZ32 = atomic do x end

waste(): ZZ32 = do
  var t: ZZ32 = 0
  for i <- seq(1#200) do t := t + 1 end
  t
end

bumpX(): () = for j <- seq(1#1000) do atomic do x := x + 1 end end

bumpU(): () = for j <- seq(1#1000) do atomic do u := u + 1 end end

run(): () = do
  do
    for i <- seq(1#100) do
      atomic do
        p: ZZ32 = readX()
        w: ZZ32 = waste()
        x := p + 1
      end
    end
  also do
    bumpX()
  end
  do
    for i <- seq(1#100) do
      atomic do
        try
          atomic do
            q: ZZ32 = u
            throw Carry(q)
          end
        catch e
          Carry => do
            w: ZZ32 = waste()
            u := e.q + 1
          end
        end
      end
    end
  also do
    bumpU()
  end
  if x = 1100 AND u = 1100 then
    println("PASS")
  else
    println("FAIL: x = " x " of 1100 after a nested block that wrote nothing, u = " u " of 1100 after a nested block that threw")
  end
end

end

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The record's tool: it owns the form of FACTS.md and POSITIONS.md and of
their two history files, and is the only way to write them.

An entry is one line under a permanent number, `- F-87 **Title.** Text.` in
explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md and `- P-48 **Title.** Text.` in
POSITIONS.md. A number is never reused or changed: a new entry takes the
highest number its file has ever used, plus one. An entry stands under the
nearest `## ` or `### ` heading above it, its section. Its title is its bold
opening, or where it has none, its opening words up to the first colon,
semicolon or full stop.

A pointer is another entry's number in the sentence that needs it, alone
(`It builds P-48.`) or with the first words of the target's title in quotes
(`It builds P-48, "A type parameter the arguments do not fix ..."`, or
`P-48 ("...")`). Quoted words must open the target's current title (`...` or
`…` marks words left out); when an entry is retitled, the tool rewrites them
in every entry that points to it, in the same call.

The history (FACTS-history.md, POSITIONS-history.md beside the record) holds,
under `### F-87`, one block per change, oldest first: one provenance line (the
UTC time from the clock, the kind of change, `from` each report section,
`commit`, `by`, then the note after a colon), and the line as it stood before
the change. The tool derives the kind: `added`, `rewritten`, `moved to "S"`,
`merged into F-n`, `F-n merged in`, `removed`, `noted`; the numbering wrote one
`numbered` block per entry. A retitle that refreshed other entries' pointer
words, or a merge that moved their pointers, says so in one more line of the
block (`pointer words refreshed in: F-12, P-48`).

A `noted` block, which `note` writes, leaves the entry as it is. It adds what
the entry's history lacks, such as the curator's messages behind a text kept
word for word, with their times, or a correction of an earlier block. It holds
no earlier line, and its note says what it adds, so it needs one. A gone entry
takes none: its last block stays `merged into` or `removed`. A noted block
that corrects an earlier block names it by its time, in the field after the
kind: `correcting the block of 2026-10-13 19:07Z`, or, where blocks of the
entry share that minute, `correcting the 2nd block of 2026-10-14 04:41Z`,
counted oldest first. The block corrected is never edited.

state it would leave, appends the history blocks first and then replaces each
record file in one step. A write is refused only for what would break the
store: a bad number, a pointer that does not resolve or whose words do not
open its target's title, a line break in an entry, no provenance (neither
`--from` nor `--note`; for a noted block, no `--note`), a correction that

Never for size. The tool does not commit: commit the record file and its
history together.
